The study was carried out in two stages and was intended to provide estimates for the entire country, for urban and rural areas in Tanzania Mainland, and for Zanzibar. The study using a stratified two-stage sample design. The first stage involved selection of sampling points (clusters) consisting of enumeration areas (EAs) delineated for the 2012 Tanzania Population and Housing Census (2012 PHC). The EAs were selected with a probability proportional to their size within each sampling stratum. A total of 629 clusters were selected. Among the 629 EAs, 211 were from urban areas and 418 were from rural areas. In the second stage, 26 households were selected systematically from each cluster, for a total anticipated sample size of 16.354 households for the 2022 TDHS-MIS. To estimate geographic differentials for certain demographic indicators, Tanzania was divided into nine geographic zones. A multi-cluster national survey stratified for the three ecological zones: Southern, Middle and Northern was carried out in 2010. The sample size and sampling design were based on the nationally representative sample used for the Food Fortification Baseline Survey in 2007. The enumeration areas (EAs), selected based on population proportionate to size (PPS) sampling methods. Each of the three major ecological zones in the country represented independent sampling frames. Within each of the eco-zones, 30 clusters, or EAs were selected by PPS. Once the 30 EAs were identified, a systematic sampling selection was undertaken to select 17 households within each. Therefore, the total expected sample size was 1530 (3 zones x 30 EAs x 17 households).

Study reported to cover the entire Cote d'Ivoire. Country stratified in three ecozones (south (forest-like vegetation),north-eastern (savannah-like) and north-western (savannah-like but with altitudes up to 1300 above sea level).The study was designed following a model-based statistic method called lattice plus close pairs sampling approach, as described by Diggle and Ribeiro (New York, USA : Springer, 2007. 228 p.). The aim was to select approximately 100 locations across Côte d’Ivoire. To apply this design, a lattice indicating latitude and longitude at a unit of 0.5° was overlaid on a map of the country showing the two major ecozones; tropical rainforest in the south (ecozone 1) and the savannah in the north (ecozone 2). Based on average population densities in the two ecozones, 58 survey locations in the southern ecozone and 42 in the northern ecozone were sampled.While most of these locations were chosen on a regular spacing using the lattice, some locations were chosen at random

National representative survey using a two stage cluster sampling covered 10 administrative regions in Ghana. Each region was separated into urban and rural areas. In the first stage, 200  enumeration areas (EAs), including 93 EAs in urban areas and 107 EAs in rural areas, were selected with probability proportional to the EA size and with independent selection in each sampling stratum. In the second stage of selection, a fixed number of 30 households was selected from each cluster to make up a total sample size of 6000 households. Replacement of non-responding households was not allowed. Survey response rate 99%.

Nationally representative survey using a stratified two-stage cluster sampling, designed to yield representative results at the national level, for urban and rural areas, and for each of the 16 regions. In the first stage, 618 target clusters were selected from the sampling frame using probability proportional to size (PPS) for urban and rural areas in each region. In the second stage, after selection of the clusters, a household listing and map updating operation was carried out in all the selected clusters, to develop a list of all the households in the cluster.

National representative survey using a two stage cluster sampling covered 10 administrative regions in Ghana. Each region was separated into urban and rural areas. In the first stage, 200  enumeration areas (EAs), including 93 EAs in urban areas and 107 EAs in rural areas, were selected with probability proportional to the EA size and with independent selection in each sampling stratum. In the second stage of selection, a fixed number of 30 households was selected from each cluster to make up a total sample size of 6000 households. Replacement of non-responding households was not allowed. Survey response rate 99%.

The survey sample for Sierra Leone was based on the provisional results of the 1974 Population Census. In Sierra Leone, apart from Freetown, was described by urban and rural groupings. The sample comprised 4880 children aged 3-59 months (0-59 months in Freetown), 3724 mothers and 1965 households.

National representative survey using two stage clustered with the SMART methodology. The first stage sample of clusters was drawn independently for each domain from the national sample frame with the support from National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) and Office of Chief Government Statistician (OCGS). The second stage of sampling consisted of selecting households within each selected cluster by using a systematic random selection procedure. Data were collected from 1081 clusters of between 16 and 20 households and 17,524 children less than 5 years of age and 9,426 women in reproductive age group were surveyed. The results are representative at national and regional levels. The 31 domains were selected based on the current administrative structure (31 regions). Ninety-nine percent of the selected clusters for children under five and for women in child bearing age were interviewed.
